doc.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Bandmates and the Buddy and Soul record
summary: He lists bandmates such as the LaBarberas, Menza, Romano, Art Pepper and Porcino, and recalls his one Rich record, Buddy and Soul. Rowe says the band was popular with college musicians.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: But he did teach me some really good — and I met all kinds of great people: The LaBarbara’s, Joe and Pat LaBarbara and Don Menza and Joe Romano and Art Pepper was on the band and Al Porcino, I roomed with Al Porcino.

Did I play? I only did one record it was kind of an awful record, it was called “Buddy and Soul.” It was sort of Buddy’s attempt at rock & roll. I think most of the tracks I ended up playing electric bass. On two or three I played string bass. But it was my first sort of big kind of project to get to do.

Well that band certainly was a big hit with the college musicians too. I mean I remember listening to and wearing those records out with my roommates. And then getting the charts and trying to play them.
